claims.statement: Per-aggregate event factories (event_factory_*.go) are the only place that constructs events; producers never hand-roll event literals. The factories are organized by concern (employee, timesheet, financial, project, system, user, advance-payment-fee, disbursement-fee, payment-cycle).

Events are persisted in the same DB transaction as the state change and published to Redis Streams post-commit via domain.RegisterAfterCommit callbacks; if the process dies between commit and publish the outbox row is still there and a sweeper republishes.

The original database outbox tables were dropped in migration 062; events now flow Redis-only and the outbox reliability guarantee is relaxed because financial correctness does not depend on event delivery.
The consumer pool uses Redis Streams consumer groups for automatic retry and dead-letter handling; sequential_handler.go orders financial events so settlement cannot overtake a payment.

The handler set (audit_event_handler, settlement_event_handler, cache_invalidation_handler, employee_user_created_handler, cash_forecast_accuracy_handler) is wired in the consumer pool; handlers are stateless and consume-then-ack with Redis retry semantics.
Two subscription shapes: Subscribe(eventType, handler) for typed routing and SubscribeAll(handler) for global handlers like the audit handler and the cache invalidator; wiring lives in bootstrap/.
